facts.statement: Psephochelys is an extinct genus of placodont reptile that lived in China during the Late Triassic.
facts.quote: Psephochelys (meaning "pebbly turtle") is an extinct genus of placodont reptile from the Late Triassic of China.

facts.statement: The genus was named in 2002 based on a single partial skeleton discovered in the Carnian-age Falong Formation in Guizhou Province.
facts.quote: named in 2002 on the basis of a single partial skeleton found in an outcrop of the Carnian-age Falong Formation in Guizhou Province.

facts.statement: Psephochelys belongs to the family Placochelyidae and the superfamily Cyamodontoidea.
facts.quote: Psephochelys is classified as a member of the family Placochelyidae, which is within the larger placodont superfamily Cyamodontoidea.

facts.statement: Psephochelys possessed a wide shell covering its body, resembling that of a turtle.
facts.quote: Like other cyamodontoids, Psephochelys has a wide shell covering its body, similar to that of a turtle.

facts.statement: Unlike other cyamodontoids, the shell of Psephochelys covered only its back.
facts.quote: However, unlike those of other cyamodontoids, the shell of Psephochelys only covers its back.

facts.statement: Psephochelys lived between 233.6 and 227.3 million years ago during the Carnian age.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Carnian (233.6 to 227.3 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Psephochelys lacked a plastron, instead having rib-like gastralia surrounded by loosely connecting osteoderms or bony plates.
rejected.quote: The plastron, which covers the underside of other cyamodontoids, is absent, and in its place are rib-like gastralia surrounded by loosely connecting osteoderms or bony plates.
